module purpose: Implements a 32-entry hardware spinlock array: it captures bus requests (bus_req_i), updates per-index lock bits (lock_q(i)) on clock edges when the request and address select an index, and drives a bus response (bus_rsp_o) that ACKs requests and returns lock state (masked by the index select).

use-case flows.value: bus request strobe (bus_req_i.stb) that begins a read or write access
write to a lock bit: update lock_q(i) from the request (lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw) under index selection
readback of lock state delivered on bus_rsp_o.data (either masked by sel when addr(7)='0' or the full lock_q vector)
bus response fields produced for each request: ack (bus_rsp_o.ack) and err (bus_rsp_o.err)
reset forces lock bits and the response port to known values

conceptual assets.concept: Bus write eligibility (per-index) — the module's decision whether a given bus request should update a particular lock_q(i)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL makes the write to lock_q(i) conditional: the spinlock process updates lock_q(i) only when (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.addr(7) = '0') and (sel(i) = '1') (guard at line 44) and sel(i) is computed from the address equality at line 51. If these inputs or the sel computation are wrong, the implemented write decision (whether a lock bit is updated) will be incorrect. Map evidence: the write guard at line 44 appears in the analyser's GATES records (bus_req_i.stb and bus_req_i.addr gate the lock update at the occurrence on line 44) and sel is computed from bus_req_i.addr at line 51 (map records show a GATED_BY on sel at the occurrence for line 51). See the related structural assets below (each entry cites the element occurrence and the map record used as the edge).

conceptual assets.concept: Spinlock state — the 32-bit register vector (lock_q) that holds each lock bit
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL implements lock state as edge-triggered registers that are reset and conditionally updated, and whose exact bit values are returned to requesters. Evidence in the RTL: lock_q(i) is reset to '0' on rstn_i (line 41-42), it is updated on the rising edge of clk_i when the write guard holds (lines 43-45: the guarded assignment lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw), and the response path returns lock_q (lines 66-70: bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel or <= lock_q). The relationship map records lock_q as a CLOCKED_BY target on the assignment at line 45 and a RESET_BY target at line 42, and shows bus_rsp_o.data deriving from lock_q at line 68 (DERIVES_FROM) and copying lock_q at line 70 (COPIES). These map records and the RTL lines establish that the integrity of lock_q is required for correct update and correct readout.
